audit_findings.title: Unfunded pension obligations may be an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.341 billion net pension and postretirement benefit obligations at 2026-06-30; approximately $1.314 billion of computed 2026 contributions
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash funding above pension expense reduces equity-level owner earnings; alternatively, any unfunded amount not borne by forecast OE is a senior claim requiring an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate making contributions to our company-sponsored U.S. defined benefit pension and postretirement medical benefit plans of approximately $1.3 billion in 2026, which are included within Expected employer contributions to plan trusts in note 5 to the audited, consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed net obligation equals 125.2% of the $5.063 billion OE anchor and 8.4% of base equity value. The 2026 contribution estimate equals 26.0% of anchor OE. Those scales can materially affect value. The omission is not yet demonstrated because pension expense is embedded in earnings and some funding may already be represented in OE; the record does not show the OE reconciliation needed to identify the uncaptured portion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 and forecast pension service cost, non-service cost, employer contributions and benefit payments to OE; then rerun using either recurring cash funding in OE or the residual funded-status claim in the bridge, without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease financing may cause maintenance investment to disappear from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $731 million of finance-lease ROU assets obtained in 2025, equal to 14.4% of anchor OE; a further $631 million was obtained in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: If maintenance investment is derived only from investing-section capital expenditures, operational assets financed through leases escape the reinvestment deduction while only depreciation and interest affect earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition to capital expenditures of $3.7 and $3.9 billion for 2025 and 2024, respectively, there were principal repayments of finance lease obligations of $133 and $136 million in these years, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: UPS obtained $731 million of finance-lease assets in 2025 but reported only $133 million of finance-lease principal payments. The asset additions were 19.8% of reported 2025 capital expenditures and 14.4% of anchor OE, so an omitted maintenance component could materially overstate recurring OE. The error is not yet demonstrated because the supplied OE workpaper does not show whether it already includes lease principal or an equivalent maintenance charge, and not every leased asset is necessarily maintenance investment.
audit_findings.action: Trace every finance-lease asset addition and principal payment through the OE calculation, classify the maintenance portion, and rerun OE with a consistent cash-equivalent maintenance charge while retaining finance-lease interest already included in equity earnings.

audit_findings.title: The NETTI withdrawal liability may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $654 million fair value at 2026-06-30, or approximately $0.76 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any portion not already borne through future OE payments should be deducted as a senior claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024 we had $ 795 and $ 804 million, respectively, recognized in Other Non-Current Liabilities and $ 9 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 recorded in Other current liabilities in our consolidated balance sheets, representing the remaining balance of the NETTI Fund withdrawal liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed fair value is $654 million, equal to 0.9% of the $75.787 billion base equity value and about $0.76 per share. A full deduction would leave the $88.27 base value near $87.51 and the $97.94 bull value near $97.18, still below the $103.50 market price; it therefore does not change the valuation conclusion by itself. Whether even that deduction is appropriate remains unresolved because future OE may already contain the liability's interest and payment burden.
audit_findings.action: Trace the approximately $9 million current balance, periodic cash payments and imputed interest through OE; deduct only the fair value of cash flows not already captured in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: Positive near-term growth may conflict with a disclosed additional volume step-down
audit_findings.magnitude: First-half 2026 net income declined 40.6%; computed adjusted net income declined 7.0% to $2.401 billion from $2.582 billion
audit_findings.mechanism: The remaining customer-volume reduction and stranded-cost removal affect first-year OE and therefore every forecast cash flow and terminal value generated from the 3% and 5% growth paths.
audit_findings.evidence: By the end of 2026, we expect that our planned volume declines from our largest customer will reduce volume by approximately one million additional pieces per day.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing says the planned reduction was completed in the second quarter, so this is no longer merely a future warning. First-half adjusted operating profit also declined a computed 5.9%, while U.S. Domestic adjusted operating profit declined 12.0%, showing that the transition materially affected current profitability despite second-quarter improvement. Applying immediate positive growth to the 2025 anchor without incorporating actual 2026 performance can therefore overstate the base and bull paths. The exact OE effect remains unestablished because interim maintenance investment and working-capital normalization are not supplied.
audit_findings.action: Build 2026 OE from filed year-to-date results plus a supportable second-half forecast, separately showing completed volume losses, USPS Ground Saver costs, stranded costs, realized savings and nonrecurring separation costs; rerun all scenarios from that first-year OE.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor does not contain a full-year contribution from the acquired perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: Perimeter inconsistency affects the OE numerator through acquired earnings, amortization, integration costs and maintenance investment, and may affect the bridge through acquired liabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: The impact of these acquisitions to our consolidated revenue and net income in 2025 was not material.
audit_findings.explanation: The $2.021 billion acquisition price is filed, but it is not a measure of omitted value. UPS stated the acquisitions were not material to 2025 consolidated revenue or net income, while first-half 2026 healthcare-logistics revenue increased $420 million from AHG and other demand and SCS operating profit increased $216 million. The filing does not isolate acquired OE, maintenance needs or assumed liabilities, so the direction and materiality of the perimeter adjustment cannot be established. Missing acquired earnings could understate value, while missing maintenance investment or liabilities could overstate it.
audit_findings.action: Prepare acquisition-date-to-present and full-year pro forma OE for Frigo-Trans and AHG, isolating recurring earnings, maintenance investment, integration costs, purchase-accounting amortization and assumed liabilities; then rerun without adding the purchase price separately.

audit_findings.title: A sale-leaseback gain could inflate the recurring OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $362 million pretax gain; filed after-tax effect of $0.30 per diluted share, approximately $255 million and 5.0% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: An unremoved after-tax gain inflates anchor OE and is capitalized through forecast cash flows and terminal value, while replacement rent remains an ongoing expense.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash proceeds of approximately $ 465 million were received and gains on sale of $ 362 million were recognized within Other (gains) losses in our statement of consolidated cash flows and within Other expenses in our statement of consolidated income.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain and its nonrecurring character are demonstrated, but its inclusion in the $5.063 billion OE anchor is not demonstrated because the OE reconciliation was not supplied. If retained, the filed $0.30-per-share effect represents about 5.0% of anchor OE. At unchanged scenario assumptions, that proportion corresponds to roughly $3.6 billion of base operating value, or about $4.17 per share, making the potential error material even though it would reinforce the existing conclusion that market price exceeds modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $362 million pretax gain and related tax effect to 2025 OE, remove all sale-leaseback and property-sale gains not already excluded, retain ongoing lease expense, and rerun the scenarios and buy-below price.
